items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I met a handsome young quiet sax player from St. Louis, Missouri named Cle Sadler. We used to drink together in Lisieux's but I never heard him play.

ctx.x: Briggs and I jammed at the Hot Feet until the wee hours of the morning and Freddie played more piano than I had ever heard. Briggs was a first chair man but he could play things at a jam session that made everybody know that he could also take hot choruses which very few first trumpet players in a trumpet section could do.
Later, during my sojourn in Paris, I met a handsome young quiet sax player from St. Louis, Missouri named Cle Sadler. We used to drink together in Lisieux's but I never heard him play.

Another famous personality that hung around the Lisieux was Spencer Williams, the composer of 'Basin Street Blues.' Kid Chocolate, the famous Cuban boxer was in Paris, so was Jimmie Monroe, the husband of Nina Ma McKinney who was one of the movie stars who played in the first all negro movie called 'Halleluiah'. Freddie 'Snake Hips' Taylor and I lived in the same hotel and Freddie was hip to gage as marijuana or reefers were called.
